# Sample WaferLens reports

Generated from real WM-811K test wafers. Pattern and confidence come from the CNN; text is written by the LLM using only the retrieved knowledge-base notes.

## Confident defect
*Test wafer #0 | true label: Center | generated by: llm*

**Pattern detected:** Center (98% confidence)

**What this usually means:**
- This pattern typically presents as a group of failed dies concentrated in the middle of the wafer [S3][S1].
- It is often associated with irregular RF operation or unusual liquid flow during processing [S1].
- It may commonly be traced to dispense and spin dynamics, or to effects at the centre of a process chamber [S2].
- It tends to point toward processes acting on a spinning or centre-fed wafer [S2].

**Suggested checks:**
- The coat and develop modules are commonly considered a primary first check [S2].
- Engineers usually confirm suspicions against the history of the tools the wafer passed through [S2].
- It is recommended to check whether the pattern repeats across several wafers or lots, as multiple maps help confirm the underlying cause [S2].

**Sources:**
- [S1] Yeonhong Kim, Jonghyeok Im, Monu Nath Baitha, Kyoungsik Kim (2026). Bridging Quantum Computing Paradigms toward Semiconductor Yield: A Controlled CV-versus-DV Comparison on Wafer-Map Defect Classification. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00961
- [S2] Averroes (2026). Wafer Defect Map Analysis: How to Read Spatial Patterns and Find Root Causes. https://averroes.ai/blog/wafer-defect-map-analysis
- [S3] Moo Hyun Kim, Tae Seon Kim (2024). Development of a Wafer Defect Pattern Classifier Using Polar Coordinate System Transformed Inputs and Convolutional Neural Networks. https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics13071360

## Uncertain prediction
*Test wafer #4 | true label: Edge-Loc | generated by: template*

**Pattern detected:** Edge-Loc (69% confidence), uncertain; possibly Edge-Ring (15%)

**What this usually means:**
- *Edge-Loc:* Often associated with irregular temperature during annealing or impurities from a load-lock valve [S1]
- *Edge-Loc:* Commonly traced to handling contact or a local fault at the edge [S2]
- *Edge-Ring:* Often associated with abnormal temperature control during rapid thermal processing (RTP) or a cold process [S1]
- *Edge-Ring:* Commonly traced to deposition and etch effects at the wafer edge [S2]
- *Edge-Ring:* A full ring points at processes that treat the edge differently by design, and the hardware around the wafer rim [S2]

**Suggested checks:**
- *Edge-Loc:* Handler and gripper logs [S2]
- *Edge-Loc:* Thermal process settings, since Edge-Loc and Scratch call for different fixes: thermal tuning for Edge-Loc, mechanical handling checks for Scratch [S1]
- *Edge-Ring:* The edge hardware of the process chamber [S2]
- *Edge-Ring:* Tool history, and whether the ring appears across several lots; a rising edge-ring rate over weeks can signal slow drift [S2]

**Sources:**
- [S1] Yeonhong Kim, Jonghyeok Im, Monu Nath Baitha, Kyoungsik Kim (2026). Bridging Quantum Computing Paradigms toward Semiconductor Yield: A Controlled CV-versus-DV Comparison on Wafer-Map Defect Classification. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00961
- [S2] Averroes (2026). Wafer Defect Map Analysis: How to Read Spatial Patterns and Find Root Causes. https://averroes.ai/blog/wafer-defect-map-analysis

## No defect pattern
*Test wafer #6 | true label: none | generated by: template*

**Pattern detected:** none (98% confidence)

**What this usually means:**
- The scattered background failures come from particles and the general process environment [S1][S2]
- These are hard to remove directly and usually need gradual environment or equipment improvements [S1]

**Suggested checks:**
- No targeted investigation is usually needed for a single wafer
- Watch the background failure rate over time; a rising rate can signal a gradual problem before it becomes a clear pattern [S2]

**Sources:**
- [S1] Moo Hyun Kim, Tae Seon Kim (2024). Development of a Wafer Defect Pattern Classifier Using Polar Coordinate System Transformed Inputs and Convolutional Neural Networks. https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics13071360
- [S2] Averroes (2026). Wafer Defect Map Analysis: How to Read Spatial Patterns and Find Root Causes. https://averroes.ai/blog/wafer-defect-map-analysis
